candidates.practical_angle: Есть новый городской контекст для Greater Manchester.
candidates.lead: A blue plaque has been unveiled in Bowdon to commemorate the life and legacy of William Wood
candidates.evidence_text: A social reformer who relentlessly campaigned against the inhumane practice of using child chimney sweeps has been honoured with a blue plaque outside his former home William Wood, who was born in 1782, was a successful wool merchant before becoming one of Britain's most determined social reformers His campaigning laid the groundwork for the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875, which finally banned the practice, but Wood did not live to see the law enacted as he died in 1868 at the age of 85 At the plaque unveiling at his former home in Bowdon, councillor Eve Parker, from Trafford Council, said Wood's "compassion, courage and lasting impact on British history will be remembered for generations to come" "William Wood's story is a remarkable piece of local history, and it's a privilege to honour his life's work," the executive member for leisure, arts, culture and heritage said "From his home in Bowdon, he fought tirelessly against unimaginable cruelty, using his own time and resources to protect vulnerable children across the country."

candidates.practical_angle: Есть новый городской контекст для Greater Manchester.
candidates.lead: The blues guitarist and vocalist Sister Rosetta Tharpe performed at an empty station for TV
candidates.evidence_text: A unique slice of Manchester's musical history - when the "Godmother of rock and roll" performed live at a city railway station - has been commemorated The day Sister Rosetta Tharpe played at the disused station at Whalley Range's Wilbraham Road in May 1964 has been marked with the unveiling of a blue plaque Tharpe, who influenced music legends Chuck Berry, Elvis Presley and Little Richard among others, was recording a show for Granada TV's Blues and Gospel Train, along with greats such as blues giant Muddy Waters The plaque is part of an initiative by social historian and broadcaster Karen Gabay, to place plaques across Manchester, honouring Black musicians who left a mark on the city It was unveiled by Gabay at Manchester Central Convention Complex - the former Manchester Central Railway Station - where Tharpe and fellow musicians boarded the train to take them to Whalley Range The historian explained: "She was one cool sister; that swagger, that strut, the way she played the guitar - so many people who see it for the first time are instantly taken aback."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The boss of Manchester Airport has defended car parking charges there, arguing they are "competitive" Chris Woodroofe was responding to a customer who asked how the airport can justify more than £150 charge for parking for two weeks The managing director said the cost was "exactly the same sort of charge" as parking in a town centre for the day, but some customers have said they felt the charges were unreasonable Manchester Airports Group (MAG) - which also includes London Stansted and East Midlands Airports - recently recorded it had made £453m from parking, about a third of its income Woodroofe told BBC North West Tonight : "If you go into the town centre and look to park for a day in the town centre and do that comparison with the £150 for two weeks, it's exactly the same sort of charge." He said the airport was competing with Uber and taxi firms as well as other parking firms

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham housing estate could be built in "beautiful" valley - BBC News Image source, IDPartnership Image caption, The development is a part of plans to build 2,000 homes in the area By Ed Barnes Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 19 August 2026 Nearly 200 homes could be built in a "beautiful" valley as part of a major development that includes a new tram stop. Barratt Homes Manchester have asked Oldham Council to approve up to 192 homes at Birshaw Farm in the Beal Valley, Oldham, Greater Manchester. It forms part of wider plans for the area, which includes around 2,000 homes, as well as other infrastructure. There is also a new road planned from Ripponden Road to Oldham Road, as well as a new Metrolink stop at Broadbent Moss. The scheme is part of the Greater Manchester Places for Everyone scheme, which aims to oversee house building, create jobs, and protect the regions's green belt land from unplanned development. The new homes would be built about three miles north of Oldham town centre and includes an area of greenfield land on the edge of Royton. The development will include wetland landscapes, green spaces, as well as accessible walking and cycling routes according to the plans , external . Image source, IDPartnership Image caption, The developers said the project would deliver £36.7m of gross value to the area Despite the loss of farmland to development, a report said the development will keep "existing woodland and mature tree groupings to establish a distinctive landscape character" with an aim to plant 551 new trees. The vision is to "create welcoming, well-connected neighbourhoods that feel part of the existing communities in Shaw, Royton, Heyside and Barrowshaw," the Local Democracy Reporting Service said. Developers also said the project would deliver 100 direct construction jobs and £36.7m of gross value added to the area. If the homes are built, they said an extra £5.5m would be spent by the homes each year with an extra £500,000 of council tax revenue. 'Irreplaceable landscape' However, concerns have already been raised in a number of comments on Oldham's planning portal. One person said: "Long-standing residents like my husband and me have intentionally stayed here for over 30 years precisely because of the strong community cohesion and the exceptional greenery of the Beal Valley. "By sacrificing this irreplaceable landscape for developer profit, the council is actively destroying the very assets that make Oldham a desirable place to live," they said. "If you take this away, there is no reason for dedicated residents to stay." candidates.lead: Plans to transform the Grade II listed theatre into "a vibrant destination" take a step forward
candidates.evidence_text: Plans to bring an historic theatre back into use have taken a major step forward after new investment was approved Wigan's Royal Court Theatre on King Street will receive part of the £3.7m funding Wigan Council is set to receive from the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, to support the borough's economy and community developments The Grade II listed theatre, which closed in 1974 and was used as a bingo hall, nightclub and bar, has already received £1.1m in funding for building works Cllr Dane Anderton said the latest funding will help bring the theatre a step closer to becoming "a vibrant destination for residents and visitors" "The Royal Court Theatre is one of Wigan's most recognisable heritage assets and we're delighted to have secured further funding to continue its revival," cabinet portfolio holder for economic development and regeneration at Wigan Council, said "The £1.1 million already invested has helped secure the building's future by carrying out vital protection and restoration works

candidates.evidence_text: Child and adolescent mental health wards at a Greater Manchester hospital that had been ordered to improve has been rated as "good" by health inspectors The Care Quality Commission (CQC) has upgraded the rating of the service at Cheadle Royal Hospital's child and adolescent mental health wards after an inspection in April The hospital, run by Affinity Healthcare Limited, provides a range of inpatient mental health services for young people between 11-17 and adults. candidates.evidence_text: A social reformer who relentlessly campaigned against the inhumane practice of using child chimney sweeps has been honoured with a blue plaque outside his former home William Wood, who was born in 1782, was a successful wool merchant before becoming one of Britain's most determined social reformers His campaigning laid the groundwork for the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875, which finally banned the practice, but Wood did not live to see the law enacted as he died in 1868 at the age of 85 At the plaque unveiling at his former home in Bowdon, councillor Eve Parker, from Trafford Council, said Wood's "compassion, courage and lasting impact on British history will be remembered for generations to come" "William Wood's story is a remarkable piece of local history, and it's a privilege to honour his life's work," the executive member for leisure, arts, culture and heritage said "From his home in Bowdon, he fought tirelessly against unimaginable cruelty, using his own time and resources to protect vulnerable children across the country."

candidates.evidence_text: A unique slice of Manchester's musical history - when the "Godmother of rock and roll" performed live at a city railway station - has been commemorated The day Sister Rosetta Tharpe played at the disused station at Whalley Range's Wilbraham Road in May 1964 has been marked with the unveiling of a blue plaque Tharpe, who influenced music legends Chuck Berry, Elvis Presley and Little Richard among others, was recording a show for Granada TV's Blues and Gospel Train, along with greats such as blues giant Muddy Waters The plaque is part of an initiative by social historian and broadcaster Karen Gabay, to place plaques across Manchester, honouring Black musicians who left a mark on the city It was unveiled by Gabay at Manchester Central Convention Complex - the former Manchester Central Railway Station - where Tharpe and fellow musicians boarded the train to take them to Whalley Range The historian explained: "She was one cool sister; that swagger, that strut, the way she played the guitar - so many people who see it for the first time are instantly taken aback."

candidates.evidence_text: Child and adolescent mental health wards at a Greater Manchester hospital that had been ordered to improve has been rated as "good" by health inspectors The Care Quality Commission (CQC) has upgraded the rating of the service at Cheadle Royal Hospital's child and adolescent mental health wards after an inspection in April The hospital, run by Affinity Healthcare Limited, provides a range of inpatient mental health services for young people between 11-17 and adults. The inspection followed the receipt of information of concern, the CQC said CQC inspectors found the hospital had made necessary improvements and was now only in breach of one regulation related to safe care and treatment At the previous inspection, inspectors found five breaches of regulation At the time of this latest review, the CQC said there were six young people admitted to the main ward and one young person in long-term segregation on another ward, which was not in general use

candidates.evidence_text: The University of Manchester Survival of iconic Lovell Telescope is key, UNESCO says as funding cuts could threaten Jodrell Bank World Heritage status Sign the Manchester Evening News campaign to save the working future of the Lovell Telescope Comment The influential United Nations committee UNESCO has thrown its support behind Jodrell Bank Observatory, as funding cuts threaten the working future of its iconic Grade I-listed Lovell Telescope In a statement issued exclusively to the Manchester Evening News , the body said it was 'premature to speculate' on whether the Government's cuts could ultimately affect the observatory's coveted World Heritage status, bestowed on Jodrell Bank in 2019 due to its significance to a UNESCO said it hasn't 'officially been notified of any development' in terms of the site's future funding, but confirmed it was attempting to liaise with 'UK authorities to gather information related to the conservation, management and future use of the property' The awarding of World Heritage status - a huge coup for countries across the world - isn't decided by a site's funding model alone But, crucially in the case of Jodrell Bank, it depends on whether a site continues to be able to operate in the manner that led to the status being awarded in the first place

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The University of Manchester Survival of iconic Lovell Telescope is key, UNESCO says as funding cuts could threaten Jodrell Bank World Heritage status Sign the Manchester Evening News campaign to save the working future of the Lovell Telescope Comment The influential United Nations committee UNESCO has thrown its support behind Jodrell Bank Observatory, as funding cuts threaten the working future of its iconic Grade I-listed Lovell Telescope In a statement issued exclusively to the Manchester Evening News , the body said it was 'premature to speculate' on whether the Government's cuts could ultimately affect the observatory's coveted World Heritage status, bestowed on Jodrell Bank in 2019 due to its significance to a UNESCO said it hasn't 'officially been notified of any development' in terms of the site's future funding, but confirmed it was attempting to liaise with 'UK authorities to gather information related to the conservation, management and future use of the property' The awarding of World Heritage status - a huge coup for countries across the world - isn't decided by a site's funding model alone But, crucially in the case of Jodrell Bank, it depends on whether a site continues to be able to operate in the manner that led to the status being awarded in the first place

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Purple Lamborghini seized by police after supercar driver's 'excessive engine revving' GMP said new powers are now available for police on the ground to prevent nusiance driving Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 16:13, 19 Aug 2026 View Image A Lamborghini supercar was taken away on the back of a truck after the driver's 'excessive revving'. Police seized the purple vehicle under new legislation to prevent anti-social behaviour involving vehicles Cops swooped to stop the purple-coloured Lamborghini Huracan on Featherstall Road in Oldham on Tuesday, Greater Manchester Police said The force said that under the new legislation, it was seized for 'anti-social driving and excessive engine revving'. An image of the sports car being loaded away was also released Under Section 59 of the Police Reform Act 2002, as amended by the Crime and Policing Act 2026, police can now seize a vehicle immediately without first issuing a warning if the legal grounds are met Previously, a warning was generally required before seizure, GMP said

He was 22 and had only been in the prison and young offender institution in Bickershaw, near Wigan , for 10 days after being transferred from HMP Forest Bank in Salford The report, published by watchdog the Prisons and Probation Ombudsman after an investigation into the tragedy, said a post-mortem examination confirmed he had taken 'psychoactive substances' before his death Ombudsman Adrian Usher said: "Although this was not found to have caused his death, psychoactive substances are known to affect mental health adversely. I am concerned that Mr Woodhead was able to obtain psychoactive substances with apparent ease at Hindley, even though strict re Concerns over roll call checks at the prison have also been raised - the report reveals he wasn't checked by an officer the night before he was found dead

Owned by Wain Estates, a public consultation is currently underway on a scheme to build around 700 homes alongside public green spaces and sports fa Commenting on the schemelast week, the club issued a statement saying: “As many supporters will know, the Lions have been developing our own vision for The Den – a community sports centre and multi-sport hub that could finally bring Swinton Lions home while creating sporting, hea View 4 Images CGI of what a new 'lion's den' stadium could look like

candidates.lead: NHS The human cost of a hospital trust under pressure: 28 deaths linked to delays at Northern Care Alliance There were 12,000 cases of delayed treatment last year at the NCA.
candidates.evidence_text: NHS The human cost of a hospital trust under pressure: 28 deaths linked to delays at Northern Care Alliance There were 12,000 cases of delayed treatment last year at the NCA. Bosses say ‘persistently high’ levels of sick leave are a major issue. Betha Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer and Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 18:29, 19 Aug 2026 Dozens of patients died or ‘came to harm’ due to treatment delays and serious errors made by staff working under extreme pressure at a Greater Manchester hospi Lengthy delays were linked with ‘28 deaths’ and 56 issues of ‘severe harm’, while problems diagnosing illness led to ten deaths last year at the Northern Care Alliance (NCA) which treats more than a million patients at hospitals in Salford , Oldham , Bury and Rochdale There were ten ‘never events’ recorded at the NCA across 2025 and 2026, which the NHS describes as patient safety incidents which were ‘wholly preventable,’ according to the trust’s own reports Concerns were also raised with maternity care, with reports highlighting an issue with increasing numbers of stillbirths recorded earlier this year There were 12,000 cases of delayed treatment last year at the NCA. Bosses say ‘persistently high’ levels of sick leave are a major issue

candidates.evidence_text: The University of Manchester Survival of iconic Lovell Telescope is key, UNESCO says as funding cuts could threaten Jodrell Bank World Heritage status Sign the Manchester Evening News campaign to save the working future of the Lovell Telescope Comment The influential United Nations committee UNESCO has thrown its support behind Jodrell Bank Observatory, as funding cuts threaten the working future of its iconic Grade I-listed Lovell Telescope In a statement issued exclusively to the Manchester Evening News , the body said it was 'premature to speculate' on whether the Government's cuts could ultimately affect the observatory's coveted World Heritage status, bestowed on Jodrell Bank in 2019 due to its significance to a UNESCO said it hasn't 'officially been notified of any development' in terms of the site's future funding, but confirmed it was attempting to liaise with 'UK authorities to gather information related to the conservation, management and future use of the property' The awarding of World Heritage status - a huge coup for countries across the world - isn't decided by a site's funding model alone But, crucially in the case of Jodrell Bank, it depends on whether a site continues to be able to operate in the manner that led to the status being awarded in the first place

candidates.lead: Northern Quarter One of Manchester's favourite murals could be ripped down It was created in 2011 by Manchester-based artist Sarah Yates.
candidates.evidence_text: Northern Quarter One of Manchester's favourite murals could be ripped down It was created in 2011 by Manchester-based artist Sarah Yates. Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 17:54, 19 Aug 2026 View 2 Images The mural on 50 Newton Stree One of Manchester’s favourite Northern Quarter murals could be ripped down under new plans The painting of a blue tit on the side of 50 Newton Street was created by artist Sarah Yates in 2011 as part of a street art project which was sponsored by Converse But plans for major repairs at the Grade-II listed historic building could see the iconic artwork taken down A planning application for the revamp of the building was submitted to Manchester council this month, and a decision to approve the plans could be made as soon as October The design statement says the plans are being led by Aroundtown SA, which describes itself online as a real estate company working in both the UK and Europe

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Purple Lamborghini seized by police after supercar driver's 'excessive engine revving' GMP said new powers are now available for police on the ground to prevent nusiance driving Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 16:13, 19 Aug 2026 View Image A Lamborghini supercar was taken away on the back of a truck after the driver's 'excessive revving'. Police seized the purple vehicle under new legislation to prevent anti-social behaviour involving vehicles Cops swooped to stop the purple-coloured Lamborghini Huracan on Featherstall Road in Oldham on Tuesday, Greater Manchester Police said The force said that under the new legislation, it was seized for 'anti-social driving and excessive engine revving'. An image of the sports car being loaded away was also released Under Section 59 of the Police Reform Act 2002, as amended by the Crime and Policing Act 2026, police can now seize a vehicle immediately without first issuing a warning if the legal grounds are met Previously, a warning was generally required before seizure, GMP said

He was remanded in custody by Judge Suzanne Goddard KC A further pre-trial hearing was scheduled for October. The prosecution was represented by Rachel Faux, and the defence by Dan Gaskell during today's (August 19) hearing at Manchester Crown Court Police were called to reports of a concern for a welfare at the property off Tweedale Street. Ms Aspinall, known to friends as Kiki, was pronounced dead at the scene

He was just 16 It followed a feud between Moston based 'M40' gang and the Rochdale and Oldham outfit Representing the Danger (RTD). Hostilities spilled out onto the streets, with 21 young men said to have been involved in total. John was killed as part of a revenge attack Ruben Candiza, 26; Valdo De-Almeida, 27; Marco Veiga, 25; and Emerson Teta, 25, had gone on trial accused of murder and violent disorder at Manchester Crown Court . Three weeks into the trial, and as their defence cases were due to begin, the four men changed their pleas to guilt Six members of the RTD gang were previously convicted of John’s murder and sentenced in 2022. Francesco Raji, now 24, of Elm Road, Oldham; Christopher Semedo, now 27, of Elm Road, Oldham; Nelson Correia, now 26, of Petworth Road, Oldham; Ismiel Correia, now 24, of Cavanagh Close

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan Young prisoner, 22, found dead in cell just 10 days after moving into prison Dylan Woodhead wasn't checked in his cell properly the night before he was found dead after he got drugs behind bars with 'apparent ease' Comments News Paul Britton Rep A young prisoner found dead in his cell was able to obtain drugs behind bars with 'apparent ease', a watchdog said in a new report which also revealed he wasn't checked properly the night before his death Dylan Woodhead died at HMP Hindley on January 8, 2021. He was 22 and had only been in the prison and young offender institution in Bickershaw, near Wigan , for 10 days after being transferred from HMP Forest Bank in Salford The report, published by watchdog the Prisons and Probation Ombudsman after an investigation into the tragedy, said a post-mortem examination confirmed he had taken 'psychoactive substances' before his death Ombudsman Adrian Usher said: "Although this was not found to have caused his death, psychoactive substances are known to affect mental health adversely. I am concerned that Mr Woodhead was able to obtain psychoactive substances with apparent ease at Hindley, even though strict re Concerns over roll call checks at the prison have also been raised - the report reveals he wasn't checked by an officer the night before he was found dead

Betha Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer and Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 18:29, 19 Aug 2026 Dozens of patients died or ‘came to harm’ due to treatment delays and serious errors made by staff working under extreme pressure at a Greater Manchester hospi Lengthy delays were linked with ‘28 deaths’ and 56 issues of ‘severe harm’, while problems diagnosing illness led to ten deaths last year at the Northern Care Alliance (NCA) which treats more than a million patients at hospitals in Salford , Oldham , Bury and Rochdale There were ten ‘never events’ recorded at the NCA across 2025 and 2026, which the NHS describes as patient safety incidents which were ‘wholly preventable,’ according to the trust’s own reports Concerns were also raised with maternity care, with reports highlighting an issue with increasing numbers of stillbirths recorded earlier this year There were 12,000 cases of delayed treatment last year at the NCA. Bosses say ‘persistently high’ levels of sick leave are a major issue

candidates.evidence_text: The University of Manchester Survival of iconic Lovell Telescope is key, UNESCO says as funding cuts could threaten Jodrell Bank World Heritage status Sign the Manchester Evening News campaign to save the working future of the Lovell Telescope Comment The influential United Nations committee UNESCO has thrown its support behind Jodrell Bank Observatory, as funding cuts threaten the working future of its iconic Grade I-listed Lovell Telescope In a statement issued exclusively to the Manchester Evening News , the body said it was 'premature to speculate' on whether the Government's cuts could ultimately affect the observatory's coveted World Heritage status, bestowed on Jodrell Bank in 2019 due to its significance to a UNESCO said it hasn't 'officially been notified of any development' in terms of the site's future funding, but confirmed it was attempting to liaise with 'UK authorities to gather information related to the conservation, management and future use of the property' The awarding of World Heritage status - a huge coup for countries across the world - isn't decided by a site's funding model alone But, crucially in the case of Jodrell Bank, it depends on whether a site continues to be able to operate in the manner that led to the status being awarded in the first place

candidates.lead: Northern Quarter One of Manchester's favourite murals could be ripped down It was created in 2011 by Manchester-based artist Sarah Yates.
candidates.evidence_text: Northern Quarter One of Manchester's favourite murals could be ripped down It was created in 2011 by Manchester-based artist Sarah Yates. Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 17:54, 19 Aug 2026 View 2 Images The mural on 50 Newton Stree One of Manchester’s favourite Northern Quarter murals could be ripped down under new plans The painting of a blue tit on the side of 50 Newton Street was created by artist Sarah Yates in 2011 as part of a street art project which was sponsored by Converse But plans for major repairs at the Grade-II listed historic building could see the iconic artwork taken down A planning application for the revamp of the building was submitted to Manchester council this month, and a decision to approve the plans could be made as soon as October The design statement says the plans are being led by Aroundtown SA, which describes itself online as a real estate company working in both the UK and Europe

Police seized the purple vehicle under new legislation to prevent anti-social behaviour involving vehicles Cops swooped to stop the purple-coloured Lamborghini Huracan on Featherstall Road in Oldham on Tuesday, Greater Manchester Police said The force said that under the new legislation, it was seized for 'anti-social driving and excessive engine revving'. An image of the sports car being loaded away was also released Under Section 59 of the Police Reform Act 2002, as amended by the Crime and Policing Act 2026, police can now seize a vehicle immediately without first issuing a warning if the legal grounds are met Previously, a warning was generally required before seizure, GMP said

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Florist handed driving ban after cutting corner and knocking 70-year-old into the air The victim sustained broken bones and spent eight days in hospital Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 13:57, 19 Aug 2026 View Image The junction of G A florist has been handed a driving ban after committing a 'careless and unsafe' manoeuvre which put a 70-year-old man in hospital for eight days Adele Shaw-Frost, 40, was behind the wheel of a white Kia Sportage on the evening of January 6 this year when she 'cut a corner' and collided with John Hogan on Penmore Close in Shaw, Minshull Street Crown Court heard today (August 19) Mr Hogan had been at the Morning Star pub in Shaw and was walking home along Grains Road with his grandson on what was said to be a dark and wet evening with snow on the ground He reached the junction with Penmore Close, less than 100ft from the pub, and began to cross the road, prosecutor Simon Barrett told the court "Ms Shaw-Frost turned right into the road in what we say was a rushed manoeuvre. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Chorlton The battle over a 'sacred' piece of Manchester is about to be won A crucial vote could take place within weeks Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 06:10, 19 Aug 2026 View 2 Images How homes planned at Ryebank Fields could look A long-running battle over the future of ‘precious’ Ryebank Fields in south Manchester could soon be over Campaigners from the Ryebank Fields Community Group believe that their planning application for the land will be put before councillors in Manchester for a vote on September 24 Their proposal is asking for the land to stay as a community woodland and meadow . It is going against a separate plan by Manchester Metropolitan University (MMU) and housing developers Step Places and the Southway Housing Trust to build 120 homes The outcome of the vote will decide the future of Ryebank Fields and the surrounding streets in Chorlton for generations to come “It is an open green space and it’s been used by the community for years and years,” said Chantal Kerr-Sheppard, a Green Party Councillor in Chorlton

candidates.evidence_text: Friday 31 July 2026 at 11:11pm More than two million voters were eligible to vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election as counting getsunderway. Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

Credit: Greater Manchester Police A man who killed a teenage boy on an e-bike after ramming him with his car has been jailed for 17 years Terrence King, 60, was found guilty of killing Devon Simmonds-Caines after deliberately driving his car into him on Rowrah Crescent in Middleton , Manchester King had been chasing the e-bike, which had been reportedly stolen, steering his vehicle directly at the teenager at speed without braking, on 22 July 2025 Emergency services immediately attended but despite their best efforts, Devon, aged 15, was died at the scene King was found guilty of murder at Manchester Crown Court on 17 July Following his death, Devon's family released a tribute , calling him a "bubbly person" who "only wanted the best for everyone around him"

Credit: via planning documents Blackley church tipped for go-ahead 19 August 2026 15:00 Dan Whelan Comments (1) World Mission Agency wants to build a 1,500-capacity church off Chain Road for its growing congregation. The plans involve the demolition of a former convent, located on a 2.5-acre Blackley site and the creation of a 57,000 sq ft, two-storey church to replace the current Winners Chapel on Salford’s Broughton Lane. The scheme would feature a 10,000 sq ft auditorium for services as well as community facilities such as classrooms and a gym. Several objections to the scheme have been lodged, many of them raising concerns about the potential for increased traffic congestion due to the number of people using the church. As a result, Manchester City Council’s highways team has recommended attendees be capped at 1,100. Manchester City Council has recommended the project for approval and its planning committee next meets on 27 August. In conclusion, the council’s planning department said the project “would enable the creation of place of worship within a well-designed modern building which incorporates facilities to meet the needs of those using their current place of worship”. Mojo Architects has drawn up the plans for the church, with Zerum acting as the planning agent. The project’s consultant team includes Miller Goodall, Tyler Grange, Orion Heritage, Arbtech, Harley Haddow, Mosodi, GIA, Roscoe Engineering, Land Studio, and Jensen Hughes. To view the application, use the reference number 141622/FO/2024 on Manchester City Council’s planning portal. At the same meeting, plans for a Jewish school on Crumpsall Lane return for another bid at approval having been rejected earlier this month. Concerns over highway safety led to councillors to commence the rejection process for the application from charity Binas Yisachar, which would have converted a former care home into two-form primary school for up to 120 children with special needs. The applicant has submitted more information relating to highways and the city council has recommended the project for approval once more. To learn more about the scheme, search for reference number 143452/FO/2025 on Manchester City Council’s planning portal. Your Comments Click here to cancel reply. Alberta opened its regulated competitive iGaming market on July 13, 2026, joining Ontario, whose market has been open since April 4, 2022. A United supporter in Canada can now watch a league reducing one of football’s most vi That creates an unusual setup for anyone following United and soccer betting from Canada. The shirt looks cleaner, but the commercial relationship hasn’t vanished. The match is the same while the betting menu can change with a provincial border In April 2023, Premier League clubs collectively agreed to remove gambling sponsorship from the front of matchday shirts after the 2025/26 season. The measure was voluntary and narrow. It applies to the front of the playing shirt, not to every place a betting company can appear a Sleeves can still carry commercial branding. Training wear remains available. Stadium boards and digital content weren’t swept away by the front-of-shirt agreement. The difference matters because 11 of the 20 Premier League clubs entered 2025/26 with gambling brands on the front Many clubs that had relied on betting money for their most valuable shirt position needed replacements at the same time, while betting companies looked for other inventory that still delivered global football exposure

candidates.lead: Dear readers — a new day, a new week, a new mayor of Manchester.
candidates.evidence_text: Dear readers — a new day, a new week, a new mayor of Manchester. But that’s not nearly the most exciting new-ness at Mill HQ today In fact, this sunny Monday marks a whole new era for our little paper, because today we welcome not one, but two new writers onto our team! God knows how we’ve managed to play Tetris with the desks in our office to make this work, but we have and they’re here now. We’ll be introd But first we have our briefing, including who is in line to replace Bev Craig as leader of Manchester City Council, in the latest election to come out of the matryoshka doll that was Burnham's Makerfield election. Plus there’s the celebs backing the re-funding of Jodrell Bank obs The sun rose this morning on Bev Craig’s Greater Manchester. Already dubbed the “Queen of the North”, the unassuming, low-ego former council leader is a departure from her predecessor Andy Burnham, though in terms of policy she is expected to continue on the same path he has set Rumours now circulate about who will be running her office. Craig has already re-appointed Burnham’s deputies, Salford Mayor Paul Dennett and former MP for Stretford Kate Green. Other names floating around for jobs in Craig’s office include former leader of Oldham Council Arooj S There will now be a council by-election in Burnage, plus a vote for the new leader of Manchester City Council. candidates.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email A blue plaque has been unveiled at a Bowdon house to mark the life of William Wood, the social reformer known as “The Climbing Boys’ Friend” The plaque is at Willow Cottage, 28 Stamford Road, where Wood lived after retiring there in 1847. It was unveiled last week at a ceremony organised by Trafford Council’s Local Studies team, attended by residents, historians, council members, Connor Rand MP and the Friends of Bowd Wood, born in 1782, was a wool merchant who began campaigning in 1826 after seeing a young boy fall to his death inside a chimney onto a live fire. “Climbing boys” were children sent up chimneys to sweep them, often suffering burns, respiratory illness, deformity and suffocation From Bowdon he funded prosecutions against master sweeps who broke child labour laws, put up placards at railway stations and wrote to newspapers He also challenged magistrates and even Queen Victoria over the use of a child sweep at Windsor Castle His work with Lord Shaftesbury included testimony to the House of Lords in 1853, which helped lead to the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875. Wood died in 1868, aged 85, seven years before the practice was banned. Six chimney sweeps from five towns carried his coffin to St Mary’s Churc

candidates.evidence_text: The first additional places are expected from September 2027 Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford Council has completed the purchase of the former Loreto Preparatory School site on Dunham Road - ending years of uncertainty over the three-acre plot and securing it for the expansion of neighbouring North Cestrian School The acquisition, funded by a Department for Education capital grant, will allow North Cestrian to add up to 300 secondary school places A feasibility study is now underway, with the first additional places expected from September 2027 and the full expansion complete by September 2028 The deal was struck by Trafford's Development and Education teams working alongside Hamblin Education Trust, which runs North Cestrian It draws a line under a two-year campaign that began when Loreto Prep - an independent Catholic primary school with a 114-year history - unexpectedly closed in July 2023 , citing declining pupil numbers and financial pressures

The annual budget increased from £2.4m to £5.5m to ensure essential A significant number of applications were received for the 2026–29 round and funding has now been allocated to 80 selected organisations Manchester is home to over 3,800 voluntary, community, faith and social enterprise organisations. Significant work has ensured this funding reaches communities who need it the most such as deprived wards, marginalised communities like disabled people and racially minoritised grou CEO Leah Chikamba-Mulando said she began the Angels of Hope for Women in 2014 because of the number of Black African women she was encountering who lacked confidence to access mainstream services in the UK Based in Gorton, the organisation became an officially registered charity in 2019, supporting women with anything from housing and immigration to benefits and domestic violence cases

candidates.evidence_text: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture From theatre, film and music to a new mural and giant fuzzy felt artwork, the projects cover a wide range of art forms and celebrate Oldham’s people, places and stories Oldham secured the Town of Culture title with its programme, Rising Up . Earlier this year, local creatives were invited to apply for a Town of Culture micro-commission. There were 84 applications, with 13 projects chosen to receive funding Some of the successful artists and groups recently came together to mark the start of the programme. Not everyone was able to attend, but all 13 projects will play an important part in Oldham’s Town of Culture year The Oldham Panorama, a famous view of the town created in 1876, is 150 years old this year. Isobel and Fay will reimagine it for today using patchwork and running-stitch embroidery Local people will be invited to add buildings and places that are important to them, using old clothes and fabric from home

candidates.evidence_text: The Council's Community Safety Service received a Closure Order for a house following reports of persistent anti-social behaviour and criminal activity The order, which is in place for three months, was granted by magistrates under the Anti-Social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014. The order makes it an offence for anyone, including the occupants, from entering the property while it is in force and restricts access only to Reports linked to the address included disorderly and intimidating behaviour, suspected drug-related activity and the order aims to provide respite to residents and protect them from disruption Closure Orders can be obtained by councils and police where a property is linked to serious nuisance, disorder or criminal activity The order will remain in place for three months initially. candidates.summary: Bolton Council is reminding local businesses not to sell disposable barbeques after the government temporarily banned them to protect homes and countryside
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits.
candidates.practical_angle: Проверить, есть ли действующие ограничения по дыму или дорожные закрытия сегодня.
candidates.lead: Bolton Council is reminding local businesses not to sell disposable barbeques after the government temporarily banned them to protect homes and countryside
candidates.evidence_text: Shops reminded not to sell disposable barbeques due to fire risk – Bolton Council Published: Wednesday, 19th Aug 2026 Bolton Council is reminding local businesses not to sell disposable barbeques after the government temporarily banned them to protect homes and countryside. Months of drought and dry weather has left countryside like a tinderbox, with firefighters welcoming the ban after serious wildfires around the country. According to government guidelines , disposable barbecues pose a significant risk to the public and the environment and "cannot be considered a safe product" in the current conditions. As a result, says the guidance, they "must not be made available for sale either in store or online at the current time" in Great Britain. The ban applies to England, Scotland and Wales, but not Northern Ireland. It comes after moorland around Greater Manchester has been plagued by wildfires all summer, with firefighters battling blazes lasting for weeks. A major incident was declared after a wildfire at Dove Stone Reservoir on Saddleworth Moor burned for almost three weeks. Although Bolton has been comparatively lucky so far this year, The Wildlife Trust for Lancashire, Manchester and North Merseyside said recently that land around Winter Hill is still recovering from devastating fires eight years ago. Parts of the country have gone 60 days with no measurable rain and even the often-damp Northwest is far drier than normal. To make matters worse, five heat waves have brought unusually high temperatures that have turned grass brown and left vegetation dry and scorched. Bolton Council’s Executive Member for Climate Change and Environmental Services, Cllr Rob Morrisey, said: “With the danger and devastation of wildfires so high this year, it’s vital that shops act responsibly and remove disposable barbeques from sale. “Experts are clear that climate change is making the likelihood of extreme weather more common and we must all do our part if we are to protect the countryside we all love. “Fortunately, retailers have responded well to the government’s instructions and I’m confident that in Bolton they will follow the guidance.” The government says it will keep the ban under review and withdraw it once changes in the weather make wildfires less likely. Retailers can find further information on the British Retail Consortium website . Cookie Consent by Free Privacy Policy website

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Council’s cabinet has approved proposals designed to boost investment, support regeneration and keep the town centre safe Plans for the ongoing redevelopment of Crompton Place and town centre CCTV were discussed at a meeting on Monday (August 17) With the demolition of Crompton Place now underway, the cabinet looked at plans to expand this key redevelopment site in the heart of the town centre The HSBC building in Victoria Square is not currently included under the current plans for demolition and redevelopment Cabinet approved the purchase of the freehold interest in 1-3 Victoria Square to allow it to be included in the transformational mixed-use redevelopment scheme In total, the net purchase cost is estimated at £1.74m with funds coming from the £100m originally set aside by the council to buy town centre properties to facilitate redevelopment

candidates.lead: Bolton Council is launching a new licensing scheme for landlords of houses in multiple occupation (HMOs)
candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Council is launching a new licensing scheme for landlords of houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) The scheme is designed to improve property conditions, strengthen management standards, and ensure tenants have access to safe, high-quality accommodation and was agreed at a meeting of Bolton Council’s Cabinet on Monday (August 17) HMOs are properties that are occupied by three or more people from different households, who share at least one basic amenity i.e. a kitchen, bathroom or toilet - the definition includes bedsits, shared houses and some self–contained flats that did not meet the required standard It is unacceptable that landlords cut corners in critical areas such as failing to obtain fire, gas, and electrical safety certificates or ensuring properties are safe Many landlords operate responsibly, but a substantial proportion of HMOs are poorly managed, unsafe and impact on the community In the past three years, the council has received 1,885 complaints about disrepair in rented homes, typically relating to fire safety, electrical and structural defects, overcrowding, cold and damp, and poor waste management and pest control

Many of these items contain batteries and valuable materials that can be recover When electrical items are placed in black and brown bins, they can also become damaged during collection and processing. This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk. By taking unwanted electricals to the correct recycling point, residents can help protect our workers, reduce waste, and ensure valuable materials are recovered and reused

candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Hidden in plain sight in Chinatown, it’s the kind of place chefs recommend, food writers praise, and regulars quietly keep going back to Jay Rayner called it “everything it should be” when he visited in 2021, which is about right. It’s intimate, informal, very good value and usually busy enough to make you feel smug if you’ve managed to get a table without waiting The pho is obviously a very good choice. So are the bánh mì. So is most of the menu, to be honest. But for the next Open Fire Dining Club , Pho Cue are stepping out of Chinatown and heading to Torr Vale Mill for something a little different They’ll be joining Tartuffe on 22 and 23 August for a menu that looks at Vietnamese cooking through a few different routes: the French influence that still runs through parts of the cuisine, the traditional use of fire found across Vietnam, and Cue’s more modern approach to Vietn There’s a continuation from the Porta dinner here too. evidence_packet.evidence_text: One of Manchester’s most celebrated restaurants has closed its doors for good, ahead of a major relaunch as an Irish pub The Allotment paved the way for vegan dining not just in our city, but across the UK, scooping up awards as it went But now the acclaimed restaurant, which stands directly opposite the magnificent Manchester Cathedral, has closed down In a statement shared online, The Allotment founder and CEO Anthony Sheridan announced that the restaurant will cease to exist in its current guise, as they prepare to invest in the future of the beautiful building Anthony has announced that in the coming months, the space will be transformed into The Sheridan Fiddle, a ‘premium Irish hospitality venue’ Soon, visitors can expect to see ‘traditional homemade Irish food, perfectly poured Guinness, carefully selected wines, live Irish music and, most importantly, the warm welcome that has always been at the heart of this venue’

candidates.evidence_text: A new exhibition coming to The Portico Library explores feminist themes of wellbeing, ageing and place in relation to magic and ritual healing Opening this October, Witches & Healers draws on Rosie Reed Hillman’s groundbreaking project Something That Was Ours , which explores what it means to be a witch today Hillman’s portraits of witches and healers are curated in dialogue with historic texts chosen by critical friends who identify with the practice of witchcraft and/or healing. The portraits, the books chosen, and their interpretation offer unique insights into the diverse lives an Using a mix of moving image and photography, the artwork builds a sensory and emotive portrait of women in midlife. Covering themes of menopause, mental health, climate change, and marital breakdown, this work explores the ways women have reclaimed the word witch and sought solac Speaking about the exhibition , Rosie Reed Hillman says: “I have worked to build rapport with contributors over the last four years and believe the intimate access conveyed in this project creates an exhibition that inspires empathy, curiosity and a greater understanding of issue “Women in midlife of all backgrounds are an overlooked demographic who want to see art and hear stories that reflect their experiences, and I hope this work speaks to them especially.”

From years spent languishing in post-industrial decline to being crowned one of ‘the coolest neighbourhoods in the world’ in the blink of an eye. What’s the story here? Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

Nevertheless, Baleba still represents Michael Carrick ’s most expensive arrival this summer following the club’s signing of two other midf United’s engine room overhaul saw Andrey Santos arrive in a £50m deal last month, while Youri Tielemans was signed for £35m. These midfield additions are reminiscent of the way the club prioritised adding three high calibre forwards in Benjamin Sesko, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeu Get the best United news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the Manchester Evening News! However, there are still some key positions that Carrick needs to strengthen before the transfer window slams shut on September 1. Perhaps the most pressing of all is the need to add a left-back to share minutes with Luke Shaw and become the veteran’s long-term successor

candidates.evidence_text: GCSE results How footballers did in their GCSE exams, including Wayne Rooney, Steven Gerrard, Frank Lampard and more Some of the Premier League's best players have taken on the exams News Liam De Brun TV and Celebrity writer 06:00, 20 Aug 2026 View 8 Images Wayne Roo Over five million teenagers are collecting their grades today as GCSE results for 2026 are announced, but how did some of the nation’s best footballers do in their exams? Students are waiting to find out what they will be doing for the next stage of their education, just a week after the A-Level results were released. The bulk of the nation can remember a summer spent worrying out how our GCSEs went GCSE results will be published from 8am (GMT) on Thursday (August 20). Students will usually receive their results in one of four ways: collection in person from school, email, an online results portal or through a dedicated results app The old A* - G GCSE grading system was replaced by a 9-1 grading scale, with 9 being the highest grade and 1 being the lowest. Fully implemented in 2020, the change was intended to make it easier for sixth forms, universities and employers to distinguish between candidates Despite finding fame at a young age, it didn’t stop some of the Premier League’s best ever footballers from having to do their exams. Due to the unpredictable nature of football, an education is vital even if you’re primed to be the next Lionel Messi

Недаром поклонники после концерт В Лондоне прозвучат песни, сопровождавшие разные поколения украинцев, будут звучать слова, в которых живут любовь, вера и несокрушимость.
